newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Rail offers up on tight supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Rail offers up on tight supply.

text.p: Some rail soymeal basis offers moved higher Wednesday in response to concern over soybean availability in the next month, merchandisers said.
"Nobody has any beans bought and there's a real scare for August," said a dealer in the southeast U.S. "There's just not a whole lot of bean coverage."
Other basis offers were supported by expectations for downtime this summer, dealers said.
Unpredictable summer weather patterns are causing volatile trade in CBOT soybean and soymeal futures, so many end-users are wary about entering cash markets, dealers said.
CBOT soybean and soymeal futures were sharply lower in response to U.S. forecasts showing rain headed for hot and dry regions of the Corn Belt by the weekend.
At 1055 CDT, CBOT August soymeal futures were down $4.40 per ton at $247.50, and other months were $3.50 to $6.00 a ton lower.
